lawyer:
AM Mahbub Uddin, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
Razik-al-Jalil, Deputy Attorney-General—For the Respondents.
parties:
Taj Nahar Begum ------ Petitioner
vs
Government of Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hussain J: In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, a Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the detenu Md Bellal Hossain, son of Farid Miah alias Sabid Miah now detained at Noakhali District Jail should not be brought before this Court so that this Court may satisfy itself that he is not being held in custody without lawful authority or in an unlawful manner. 

 The petitioner is the wife of the detenu and, as such, she is entitled to file the instant Writ Petition. On 3-10-2000, the Officer-in-Charge of Sonaimuri Police Station, District Noakhali arrested the detenu from his house in connection with GD No. 104 dated 3-10-2000 of Begumgonj Police Station under section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC). After that, he was produced before the Magistrate, 1st Class, 2nd Cognisance Court, Noakhali with a forwarding report alleging that while living in Kuwait, the detenu killed the old father of his employer and after that, escaped from Kuwait by creating a forged passport in the name of another person. He came to Bangladesh and was on the run to avoid arrest by the police. The Officer-in-Charge received several memoranda from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of Bangladesh through the Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali to arrest the detenu. The detention was declared illegal by the High Court Division as evidenced by the order dated 11-1-2001 of the Court of Magistrate, Noakhali. The detenu has since been confined in custody under section 54 of the CrPC. On behalf of the detenu several applications for bail were moved before the Magistrate, 1st Class, Noakhali but those applications were rejected without assigning any reason. The detenu filed Miscellaneous Case No. 499 of 2006 before this Court under section 498 of the CrPC. A Division Bench of this Court issued Rule and ultimately, the Rule was made absolute on 22-6-2006 directing the District Magistrate to release the detenu on bail. In spite of receiving that order, the learned Magistrate did not enlarge the detenu on bail as is evident from the order dated 20-7-2006 (Annexure-B). Although the learned Magistrate and the Jailor, Noakhali District Jail received a copy of the judgment and order dated 22-6-2006 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous. Case No. 499 of 2006, they did not release the detenu from custody. Subsequent orders passed by the learned Magistrate revealed that the detenu was being detained on the basis of a warrant of arrest issued by a Court of Kuwait in Felony No. 132/99. The Government claimed that the detenu was a life-convict in a criminal case in Kuwait. Admittedly, there is no 'Extradition Treaty' between Bangladesh and Kuwait to date. The Court of Magistrate and the Ministry of Home Affairs are in the dark about the law applicable to the case. The Government's stand regarding the matter is not clear. As a result, the detenu cannot be detained for an indefinite period. 

 3. Respondent No. 1 filed an affidavit-in-opposition. The case of respondent No. 1, in short, is that the detenu Bellal was accused in a murder case in Kuwait being Felony Case No. 132 of 1999. On 13-6-2001, Kuwait Embassy in Dhaka requested the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to extradite Bellal to Kuwait. Pursuant to that request the detenu was first arrested under section 54 of the CrPC. After wards, the learned Magistrate, 1st Class and Cognisance Court No. 1, Noakhali issued custody warrant showing him arrested in Felony Case No. 132 of 1999 of Kuwait. Mean-while, this Court issued Rule on 22-2-2006 and directed release of the detenu on bail in Criminal Miscellaneous. Case No. 499 of 2006. On 20-7-2006, the District Magistrate accepted the bail bond but the detenu was kept in custody in connection with Felony Case No. 132 of 1999 (Kuwait). Kazi Miraj Hossain, Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka recorded statement of detenu Bellal under section 164 of the CrPC on 12-6-2000. In the confessional statement, the detenu admitted committing murder in Kuwait. The District Magistrate, Noakhali by a memo dated 3-12-2006 issued a memo to the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs seeking guidelines of what to do about Bellal. Admittedly, there is no 'Extradition Treaty' between Bangladesh and Kuwait. However, a process is going on to include Kuwait as 'Treaty State' in the Extradition Act, 1974 (in short, the Act). On the charge of murder, the detenu was convicted and sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life by a Criminal Court of Kuwait. Therefore, it is necessary to confine him in jail so that in due course, he can be extradited to Kuwait authority. In order to keep good relation with the Government of Kuwait, it is necessary to extradite detenu to the Kuwait authority as soon as the Extradition Treaty is finalised. 

 6. We have considered the Writ Petition, its annexures and the affidavit-in-opposition. Admittedly, the detenu was arrested under section 54 of the Criminal Procedure Code in connection with GD Entry No. 104 dated 3-10-2000. Later, the detenu was shown arrested in Felony No. 132/1999 (Kuwait) in pursuance of a warrant of arrest issued by a Court of Kuwait as evidenced by the order dated 8-11-2001 passed in Serial No. 75 of 2000 of the Court of 1st Class Magistrate and Cognisance Court No. 3, Noakhali. Record reveals that the detenu was taken on remand on 4-10-2000 for four days. On 11-10-2000, pursuant to a memo dated 10-10-2000 of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Officer-in-charge Begumgonj Police Station, Noakhali prayed for seven days remand of the detenu and the prayer was allowed. The order dated 16-10-2000 shows that the confessional statement of the detenu was recorded by a Metropolitan Magistrate Dhaka and the detenu was confined in custody in Dhaka for a long time. Later, he was again taken back to Noakhali. From the affidavit-in-opposition, it appears that no committal proceeding under section 6 of the Act was initiated. It would be pertinent to have a glimpse over section 6 of the Act as under: 

 10. Section 12 of the Act provides that if a fugitive offender, who, has been taken into custody to await his surrender, is not conveyed out of Bangladesh within two months after such committal, the High Court Division may order such prisoner to be discharged unless sufficient cause is shown to the contrary. 

 13. It seems that the provision of section 4 of the Act escaped the notice of the Ministry of Home Affairs. After more than 7 years it would not be proper to give an opportunity allowing the Government to initiate a committal proceeding under section 6 of the Act after making a notification in the official gazette directing application of the provisions of the Act in relation to Kuwait. While enlarging the detenu on bail in Miscellaneous Case No. 499 of 2006 the High Court Division, amongst other things, stated as follows: 

 14. Record reveals that taking the plea of custody warrant issued by a Court of Kuwait, the detenu was not released from custody. In this connection, we would like to refer to the case of Abdul Abedin Abdul vs State 53 DLR 109. The facts of the case are quite distinguishable from those of the present case. Even then, in that case it was held that the fugitive prisoner might be extradited from Bangladesh to the United Kingdom in the manner as stated under section 6 of the Act. 

 17. Considering all aspects of the case, we are of the view that the detenu has been detained in custody pursuant to a warrant of arrest of a fugitive offender issued by a Court of Kuwait for an indefinite period without lawful authority. 

 18. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute and the detention of the detenu in connection with (Serial No. 75/2000) warrant of arrest issued by a Court of Kuwait is declared to be without lawful authority and the detenu has been detained in custody in an unlawful manner.
